title: A reversal score separates two Markov interval models with equal expected burst counts
abstract: We developed a directional control for the long-silence burst rule. We prove that two stationary three-category Markov interval models have equal expected forward burst counts for every record length. One is reversible and the other has a directed cycle. The forward-minus-reversed score separates them. Its expectation equals a stationary probability current times an explicit finite-length factor. An exact independent-record reversal test allows arbitrary reversible dependence within records. In 1,000 synthetic experiments per model, its two-sided rejection rate at 5% was 5.3% for independent intervals, 4.9% for reversible alternation, and 100% for the directed cycle. The dependent models had similar positive excess over a global interval shuffle. All 29,524 category sequences through length nine passed count checks. The score misses symmetric bursts and does not control irreversible state drift. No new mouse data or channel mechanism is established. Code, proof, simulation draws and provenance are included.

display.caption: Synthetic tests with 12 independent records of 600 intervals per experiment. Left: mean shuffle excess and reversal score. Right: exact reversal test rejection rates over 1,000 experiments, with 95% Wilson intervals. The null requires reversal invariance, not interval exchangeability.
